profile.name: Ronit Baniya Gupta
profile.slogan: if it doesn't exist, I will build it
badges: Bachelor of Computer Engineering — Pokhara University

principles.title: Originality over everything
principles.note: No copy-paste ideas. If someone already made it, I make it better or I don't make it.

principles.title: Build it, then improve it
principles.note: I'd rather ship a rough working thing today than a perfect thing next year.

principles.title: Brutally honest feedback
principles.note: Tell me I'm wrong and why. Comforting lies never built anything.

principles.title: Hardware + software, together
principles.note: The interesting problems live where the code touches real wires and real world.

journey.title: Started Diploma in Computer Engineering
journey.note: First time I held an Arduino, I was done for.

journey.title: First builds
journey.note: RC cars, relays, IR remotes. Learning by frying things.

journey.title: Air Mouse wins PEC Tech Expo
journey.note: First award. Confirmed I wanted to build weird things for a living.

journey.title: SurakshaGhar — home automation at scale
journey.note: Full ecosystem: firmware, PCB, companion app. My first real product.

journey.title: Suraksha360 sweeps hackathons
journey.note: GCES IT Expo, UDAAN, OCTATE. Best of best, multiple award categories.

journey.title: Now
journey.note: Swasthya Sathi, GRAVAS, SwiftIgnite v2, restaurant websites, and whatever breaks next.

fun_facts: 3rd DAN Black Belt in Taekwondo — started BS 2070, stopped, came back, finished high-performance coach training.
Weak at theory, strong at shipping. I learn better with a screwdriver in my hand.
Wanted to be a teacher once. Explicitly not anymore. Building a company instead.
I send cold messages to restaurants to build their websites. It works sometimes. I keep iterating.

projects.title: Suraksha360
projects.description: My biggest ecosystem to date. Started as a home-security project and grew into a full emergency-response platform — IoT sensors, wearables, healthcare and AI stitched together. Won Best of the Best at UDAAN 2025 and swept multiple award categories.

projects.title: Swasthya Sathi
projects.tagline: Healthcare platform with AI symptom checker
projects.description: A healthcare platform I'm building — AI symptom checker, digital health records, doctor finder, emergency assistance and IoT integration. Health data in one place, connected to hardware where it counts.

projects.title: SurakshaGhar
projects.description: My home automation ecosystem — 4-channel relay switch, RFID door lock, PIR detection, web control and a companion app. I designed the PCB in EasyEDA, flashed the firmware, and took it from breadboard to production switch.

projects.title: SwiftIgnite
projects.description: Motorcycle keyless ignition — Bluetooth + relays + battery management in one board. Version 2 adds live GPS tracking, SIM800L telemetry and an SMS database so you always know where your bike is.

projects.title: GRAVAS
projects.description: My Bachelor's major project — a robotic arm that follows your hand using MediaPipe hand tracking. No gloves, no markers. Python reads your hand, pyFirmata moves the servos.
highlights: Defended in front of a panel

projects.title: Air Mouse
projects.description: One of my earliest projects — control the cursor by moving your hand in the air. Basically told me which direction I was going in.

projects.title: AEGIS
projects.description: A large-scale disaster-response concept — smart city, robots, drones, sensors, AI and a central command center all talking to each other. The next thing I want to exist.

projects.title: Call-Based Motor Control
projects.tagline: Turn motors on/off with a phone call
projects.description: A product I took to market in May 2025 — control industrial/agricultural motors with a simple phone call. No internet needed, no app, no subscription. Built for places where WiFi doesn't reach.

projects.title: Ghostware360: Debug or Die
projects.description: A horror-puzzle game where debugging is the gameplay. You're a developer trapped in a haunted codebase. Still being built — because who doesn't want to turn debugging into a horror story.

projects.title: Smart Parking System
projects.tagline: Parking that tells you where to go
projects.description: IoT parking system — sensors detect free slots and point drivers to them instead of circling forever.

projects.title: RC Car Builds
projects.tagline: Rc_Car1, Rc_Car2 & the NRF stealth version
projects.description: A whole garage of RC cars — Rc_Car1 and Rc_Car2 plus a stealth variant that swapped IR for NRF radio modules, so it actually works outside the living room.

projects.title: GPS Tracker & Buck Converter
projects.tagline: Track a thing, power it properly
projects.description: Two-in-one hardware exercise — a working GPS tracker plus a custom buck converter to power it from a battery properly.

projects.title: Lyrics Display Systems
projects.description: A whole series of lyric display builds — OLED and LCD boards that fetch song lyrics from the internet and scroll them in real time. Music on hardware. Ten-plus songs, ten-plus variants.

projects.title: Fishtail
projects.description: My experimental workspace — a mix of dev-core software and raw hardware experiments. The drawer where projects start before they get names.

projects.title: M.A.M.A
projects.description: Concept + prototype for a multi-agency management assistant — one dashboard for agencies that never talk to each other.

projects.title: HerLegal
projects.description: A legal information site — static front-end with Supabase for content. Early web work while I was learning how the other half of software lives.

projects.title: Bulk QR Generator
projects.tagline: Hundreds of QR codes, one script
projects.description: A Python tool that turns a CSV into hundreds of QR codes in one run. Built because I needed it, the way all good tools get built.

projects.title: RUDRA-1
projects.description: A robotics project built around cameras and vision, complete with full project proposal documentation. Won the 9th PEC Tech Expo.

projects.title: A.I.R.I.S.
projects.description: My own voice assistant — speech-to-text, text-to-speech, command handling, all wired together locally. Half product, half training my Python.

projects.title: USB Rubber Ducky builds
projects.description: USB keystroke-injection experiments with a Rubber Ducky. Security research — knowing how these work is how you defend against them.

projects.title: SmartDustBin
projects.description: A smart dustbin firmware — sensors and automation so the bin handles itself. Small project, big lesson in keeping things simple.

projects.title: SlideSmart
projects.description: Curtain automation you drive from your phone. Press a button, curtains slide. The boring problems are the ones worth automating.

projects.title: Custom Buck Converter
projects.description: A custom buck converter I designed — dropping battery voltage down cleanly for the boards that need it. Power electronics is where projects live or die.

projects.title: Custom Relay Module
projects.description: A relay module I designed myself rather than buying off the shelf — the kind of component that shows up in half my other projects.

projects.title: Earthquake Simulator
projects.description: A Flask app that visualizes earthquakes — plotting the ones that already happened and simulating the ones that might. Web + Python in one project.

projects.title: Mass Report (TikTok Bot)
projects.description: A Python reporting bot that handles mass reporting on TikTok. Built to automate something that was taking hours by hand.

projects.title: Home Automation Lab
projects.description: My self-hosted home-automation lab — light sensors, ultrasonic triggers, relay boards and ESP32 wroom modules. The sandbox where home automation got figured out.

projects.title: WiFi Tracking & CSI
projects.description: WiFi tracking experiments — RuView for device detection and channel-state-information capture to understand what WiFi can see. A deep rabbit hole.

projects.title: ESP Utility Toolkit
projects.tagline: MAC finder, pin checker, tag victim
projects.description: A pile of small but essential ESP utilities — finding MAC addresses, checking pin layouts on nRF boards, and a Lager Tag victim build. The unglamorous tools every build depends on.

projects.title: RoomLightApp
projects.description: A room-light control app — early attempt at putting my hardware behind a phone interface.

projects.title: Diploma CTEVT Checker
projects.description: A desktop app that checks Diploma CTEVT results — packaged into a real .exe with PyInstaller so batch-mates could run it without touching Python.

projects.title: Restaurant Websites (ROS)
projects.tagline: Butter Mellow, Ember & Ivy, Nako Cafe & more
projects.description: A string of restaurant websites I designed, built and deployed — Butter Mellow Cafe, Ember & Ivy, Foxy's Corner, Nako Cafe Lakeside, Newari Bhatti and a few others. This is also where I learned cold outreach: message a restaurant, build them a site, iterate on the pitch until one says yes.

projects.title: PahiloMart WebPage
projects.description: A web-store landing page built with Vite + TypeScript + Tailwind and deployed behind Netlify redirects. Modern front-end stack, real product intent.

projects.title: Group Minor Project (PHP)
projects.description: College group project — a PHP login/signup system running on XAMPP. My first taste of auth, sessions and why the back-end hurts.

projects.title: Self-Hosted n8n
projects.description: n8n self-hosted in Docker — my own workflow automation server. I like owning the tools I depend on.

projects.title: Home Motor Timer
projects.tagline: Motor on for 6 hrs, off for 1 min, repeat
projects.description: A real-world household problem solved — a timer that runs a home motor on a strict cycle so it never burns itself out. Built because home needed it.

projects.title: AI Agents & Hand Detection
projects.description: An experimental stack — REAL_AGENT and AI AGENT scripts plus hand-detection demos. The AI/vision layer of what becomes bigger things.

projects.title: JAVA Practical
projects.description: My semester Java practical work — the theory-heavy half of engineering. I learn better with a soldering iron, but Java got drilled in anyway.

projects.title: ESP-IDF Hello World
projects.description: The very first ESP-IDF experiments — Day 01, Test, hello_world — with CMake, sdkconfig and a pytest hello-world test. Every big project starts with a blinking LED.

projects.title: Cloned & Scraped Websites
projects.description: A folder of cloned and scraped sites — royevent.com, Gandaki Tent & Decoration, sagarmathapokhara.edu.np, SlayerCloudSite and saved pages from box.com, dropbox, icloud and google. How I reverse-engineered websites before I could build my own.

projects.title: D:\app — Next.js App
projects.description: A bare Next.js app — layout, page, not-found and globals. Early experiments with the App Router that later grew into real sites.

projects.title: Computer Graphics
projects.description: Semester computer graphics work — the math and code behind rendering things to a screen.

projects.title: Assembly Level Coding
projects.description: Assembly-level programming and VHDL coursework — getting down to where the processor actually lives. Painful, educational, useful once.

projects.title: Project05 PA
projects.description: One of my home-lab mini projects — the kind of thing I built on the workbench between real projects.

projects.title: College Semesters (PEC)
projects.description: The full BE college archive — semester folders from BE.PEC and PEC with notes, presentations and exam prep. The paperwork side of engineering.
